texts: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a genetically diverse disease: well over a thousand mutations in more than ten genes, mostly genes of the sarcomere, can cause it: D.
In the picture, many different recipe books on the shelf all make bodybuilders.
Under the microscope the hypertrophied fibres are in disarray, in disorganised whorls, not arranged in parallel sheets.
Most cases are familial, inherited as an autosomal dominant trait, so half of a patient's children are at risk: the family tree.
Genetic testing begins with the affected patient; relatives are tested for the mutation once one is found, and all first-degree relatives are screened clinically.
Memory hook: many recipe books, tangled fibres, and a family tree.
